note: The ONE canonical Situation Map. Manual (restructure/frags/pocket.html), Field Kit pages 5-6 and the Field App (src/data/situations.ts) all take their wording from this file. answer = full first move (App); kitRow = the same move without the leading tool name (Kit laminate and Manual map, after the tool names). tools[0] is the primary tool; tools[1] the second.
rule: Read from the top and take the first row that matches. Several at once? Safety comes first.
footer: Flooded part-way through any row? Back to Pause + Return. Afraid at any point? Back to the first row: Pause + Return is for flooding, never for fear.
floods: At any point, if someone floods: take a Pause + Return, then restart warm. If threats, fear, coercion or violence appear, do not return at the set time: leave safely and use the Help Lines.

rows.question: I’m afraid, being threatened, or not free to say no
rows.description: You’re afraid of your partner, or being threatened, pressured or controlled, and it’s more than a hard conversation.
rows.mapNote: This includes jealousy that leads to checking, restricting or accusing. Numbers are not on this map: keep them somewhere private.
rows.answer: Stop. These tools are not for this. Get outside help (see Help Lines). Immediate danger: your local emergency number.
rows.kitRow: Stop. These tools are not for this. Get outside help (see Help Lines). Immediate danger: your local emergency number.

rows.question: I’m flooded or shut down (but safe)
rows.description: Racing heart, tunnel vision, can’t think straight, urge to flee or win.
rows.mapNote: Racing heart, urge to flee or win.
rows.answer: Pause + Return, with an exact return time. For flooding, never for fear. If you’re the one waiting: don’t follow or message.
rows.kitRow: Exact return time. For flooding, never for fear. If you’re the one waiting: don’t follow or message.

rows.question: A fight is starting
rows.description: Voices are rising and you’re both building a case.
rows.mapNote: Voices rising; you’re both building a case.
rows.answer: 60-Second Reset. Say: “I want to connect, not fight. Can we talk at ___?” Too hot to stay in the room? Pause + Return. Next: the System Overlay, and start it with the Green Rule.
rows.kitRow: Say: “I want to connect, not fight. Can we talk at ___?” Too hot to stay in the room? Pause + Return. Next: the System Overlay, and start it with the Green Rule.

rows.question: Outside pressure or disapproval from family, friends or strangers
rows.description: Family disapproval, discrimination or judgement from others is landing on the two of you.
rows.answer: Team Agreement: decide together how the two of you respond. Never limit a partner’s contact with anyone. Pressure coming from your partner? If they check, restrict or punish your contact with others: row 1 (Help Lines). Otherwise: the Green Rule.
rows.kitRow: Decide together how the two of you respond. Never limit a partner’s contact with anyone. Pressure coming from your partner? If they check, restrict or punish your contact with others: row 1 (Help Lines). Otherwise: the Green Rule.

rows.question: Trust breach
rows.description: Lying, infidelity or a broken agreement: something the partner agrees they did.
rows.answer: Safety first, then Trust Recovery. A breach is something the partner agrees they did. Seeing friends or family, privacy or a locked phone is never a breach. Skip Your First Week: start with Trust Recovery, then the Weekly Reset. Agree one change you’ll both see, and check it together at a set time.
rows.kitRow: Safety first. A breach is something the partner agrees they did. Seeing friends or family, privacy or a locked phone is never a breach. Skip Your First Week: start here, then the Weekly Reset. Agree one change you’ll both see, and check it together at a set time.

rows.question: Pulling away
rows.description: Warmth missing, repairs on autopilot: several signs of pulling away, not just needing space.
rows.answer: Check-Up: each of you marks your own half of the sheet, privately. Contempt, fear or coercion: stop and get outside support first. A partner who has stopped sharing because they are afraid is not pulling away: use the Help Lines. Then, only if you both want one: Full Repair.
rows.kitRow: Each of you marks your own half of the sheet, privately. Contempt, fear or coercion: stop and get outside support first. Stopped sharing out of fear? Help Lines. Then, only if you both want one: Full Repair.

rows.question: After a fight, or something small stung
rows.description: Something sharp was said, or a small promise slipped, and it’s still sitting there.
rows.answer: Micro-Repair: start within minutes if you can; finish within 24 hours. Bigger hurts go to Full Repair.
rows.kitRow: Start within minutes if you can; finish within 24 hours. Bigger hurts go to Full Repair.

rows.question: We keep clashing the same way
rows.description: Reach–Recoil (one reaches, the other pulls back), the same ask on repeat, or one of you always wanting to talk sooner than the other.
rows.answer: Name it out loud: “I think we’re doing the thing again.” Later, when you’re calm, find the pattern in the Manual’s Appendix A and try Profile Calibration together. Also: Check-Up.
rows.kitRow: Name it: “I think we’re doing the thing again.” Later, when calm, find the pattern in the Manual’s Appendix A and try Profile Calibration together. Also: Check-Up.

rows.question: Intimacy feels stuck
rows.description: Asking or saying no feels tense; things have gone cold.
rows.answer: Intimacy Pact. Pressure after a no: stop; don’t talk it through in the moment. The person pressured decides whether, when and with whom to talk. Force, threats, fear or a repeat: Help Lines.
rows.kitRow: Pressure after a no: stop; don’t talk it through in the moment. The person pressured decides whether, when and with whom to talk. Force, threats, fear or a repeat: Help Lines.

rows.question: Saying one thing, doing another
rows.description: Your own follow-through: promises that don’t match what happens.
rows.answer: Consistency Pact: a private weekly check. Broke a shared agreement? Tell your partner. After a breach (something the partner agrees they did)? A Proof item only if you both agree.
rows.kitRow: A private weekly check. Broke a shared agreement? Tell your partner. After a breach (something the partner agrees they did)? A Proof item only if you both agree.

rows.question: We feel like housemates
rows.description: Conversations are just logistics; the connection feels thin.
rows.answer: Daily Rhythm: a morning hello and an evening catch-up. Still thin after two weeks? A Check-Up. Feels like a chore? Take a night off fixing: a Sun Memory.
rows.kitRow: A morning hello and an evening catch-up. Still thin after two weeks? A Check-Up. Feels like a chore? Take a night off fixing: a Sun Memory.

rows.question: Time for our weekly check-in
rows.description: A short catch-up at a set time, to keep small things small.
rows.answer: Weekly Reset: about 40 minutes (15 is fine to start). The monthly part adds 10 minutes.
rows.kitRow: About 40 minutes (15 is fine to start). The monthly part adds 10 minutes.
